80340.subject: Ethereum’s Last Moat
80340.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Ethereum’s last moat is slowly fading away. You can argue that Ethereum has been losing the trading race to Solana, Hyperliquid, and more recently Robinhood Chain. But the response has always been fairly straightforward: Ethereum still has the liquidity.

And historically, that has been a good response. Trading activity can move quickly. Deep stablecoin liquidity and established lending markets have been much harder to displace. Ethereum has remained the place where a huge amount of crypto’s capital sits, and where its most established applications put that capital to work.

There are three reasons why I think that will change going forward.

**First, the most exciting growth stories in DeFi are happening entirely outside of Ethereum.**

Tokenized equities are the best example. Stablecoins grew from essentially nothing into a roughly $300B market. Equities are the next major wave of assets moving onchain, although the trajectory will obviously be different.

With equities, issuance is a necessary first step but not the main goal. People want to trade equities, finance positions, and borrow against them. Look at tokenized equity trading volume by chain in the chart below. The race is between Solana, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, and Base. Ethereum is not just losing here; it’s not even competing.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9bc58482-177b-43df-9f2f-58cd87b63c54/image.png?t=1791249847)
Caption: 

The funny thing is, Ethereum has a larger share of tokenized equity supply than Solana, Robinhood Chain, and Base. I’m sure some people will point to this metric to argue that I’m cherry-picking the data. I would then ask: how is Ethereum’s tokenized equity supply being used? As we saw, it’s barely being traded: DEX volume in the past 30 days was just $25M, equivalent to roughly 3% of outstanding supply, compared with 4.7x supply turnover on BNB Chain and 7x on Solana.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/021205b1-4994-4091-830d-aec70daddd9c/image.png?t=1791249848)
Caption: 

Alright, so if it’s barely being traded, maybe it’s deposited as collateral on lending protocols? Not really. 

Lending, like trading, is also happening outside of Ethereum, and this is more worrying. Look at Aave. Its Equities Hub launched on Base, with seven Coinbase tokenized equities accepted as collateral. Aave, which I would consider Ethereum’s most successful application, will see the growth of equity collateral happen on Base.

80332.subject: 🕵️ ZachXBT infiltrates Chinese crime syndicate
80332.body:
———————————————————————————

## Top Stories

**BTC** $86,233 (0.2%) | **ETH** $2,710 (-0.1%) | **SOL** $120 (-0.2%)

* ZachXBT says he infiltrated a Chinese crime syndicate that laundered more than $1 billion for [Lazarus Group](https://x.com/zachxbt/status/2107081638073319437)

* OpenAI is in talks with UAE funds, including MGX, for a [$30B-plus round](https://cryptobriefing.com/openai-seeks-30b-funding-at-14t-valuation-with-uae-blackrock-bloomberg/) at a $1.4T pre-money valuation

* The US Treasury withdraws two proposals targeting [unhosted wallets](https://x.com/AggrNews/status/2107099466805211307) and crypto mixing

* Solana launches an open-source [DvP program](https://x.com/DecryptMedia/status/2107290306613846152) for institutional trade settlement with J.P. Morgan input

* Ondo Finance launches tokenized notes tied to private tech companies, starting with a [pre-IPO AI firm](https://x.com/Cointelegraph/status/2107372965566333323)

* S&P Global Ratings launches a risk assessment framework for onchain lending vaults as sector deposits reach [$10 billion](https://cryptobriefing.com/sp-global-ratings-onchain-lending-vaults/)

* Strategy bought [334.3 BTC](https://x.com/solidintel_x/status/2107077494763405597) worth about $29 million — Posts its [first quarterly profit](https://x.com/business/status/2107087160968962117) in four quarters as Bitcoin rally drives $21 billion Q3 gain

* OKX launches OKX Money, a stablecoin app where qualifying USDG balances earn [up to 10% APY](https://cointelegraph.com/news/okx-money-stablecoin-savings-payments-emerging-markets) — Raises capital at a [$25B valuation](https://x.com/WuBlockchain/status/2107445766776390046?s=20)

* Chainalysis finds wallets sending P2P stablecoin transactions in China grew [43x](https://cointelegraph.com/news/china-stablecoin-p2p-wallets-crypto-restrictions) from Q1 2024 to Q2 2026

* Moonshot AI closes final private round at [$50 billion valuation](https://x.com/business/status/2107301072951738829) targeting a Hong Kong IPO in early 2027

* DeepSeek is close to securing at least [$12 billion](https://cryptobriefing.com/deepseek-nears-12-billion-funding-2027-ipo/) ahead of planned early 2027 IPO

* Stripe plans to expand stablecoin cards to [over 100 countries](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/10/01/stripe-to-expand-stablecoin-cards-to-over-100-countries-by-the-end-of-the-year) by year-end

* DeFi Development Corp adds about 26,203 SOL between Sept. 28 and Oct. 2, reaching roughly [2.56 million SOL](https://x.com/solananew/status/2107090293254410447)

* Tech billionaires drive all 2026 gains on Bloomberg Billionaires Index as non-tech members lose a combined [$62 billion](https://x.com/business/status/2107058223916183603)

* CFTC reportedly proposes its first [formal crypto market rules](https://x.com/solidintel_x/status/2107131516807426311), replacing enforcement-only approach with new CTX and CAM regulations
